snp5.2:2.3: The Thai edition notes that this word is excessive for the line’s meter.
snp5.2:3.1: Per Nd II, the streams that “flow every which way” are the streams of craving, views, conceit, defilement, corruption, and ignorance flowing out through the six sense media. This opening half-line of Ajita’s second set of questions is identical to the opening half-line of Dhp 340.
snp5.2:6.6: See DN 11, DN 15, MN 49, and SN 12:67. Asaṅga, in the Yogācārabhūmi, quotes a Sanskrit version of this sutta that inserts at this point the final question-and-answer on how consciousness itself is brought to a halt — the exchange that, in the Pali, instead appears at the end of Sn 5:13. A Sanskrit manuscript found at Turfan contains the same insertion at the same point, along with traces of other insertions.
snp5.2:7.4: In SN 12:31 the Buddha puts this same question to Ven. Sāriputta, who, with some prodding, gives an answer the Buddha endorses. A learner, he says, rightly sees that each of the aggregates has come into being, has arisen from a specific nutriment, and would cease with the cessation of that nutriment, and trains for disenchantment with, dispassion toward, and the cessation of each in turn. One who has fathomed the Dhamma sees the same three things but is already released — through disenchantment, dispassion, cessation, and freedom from clinging — from what has come into being, from its nutriment, and from its liability to cease.
